title: SE(n)-Invariant Flow Matching: A General Framework with Application to Object Reassembly
claim: Global symmetry makes naive learning one-to-many via redundant orbits; fixing a canonical section and projecting out vertical drift makes it one-to-one.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right; manifold sketches in B and C contrast, with dashed separators
description: Three panels separated by dashed vertical lines. Panel A shows flow matching on puzzle pieces: a blue random state box at t=0, a middle gradient box with gray streamlines converging to an assembled puzzle and an arrow for 0<t<1, and an orange final-state box at t=1. Panel B shows a curved, shaded manifold with dashed yellow group orbits. A blue noisy-state point sends red dashed arrows toward green dots along an orbit, each with a puzzle in a different orientation, labeled Non-identifiable Global Drift, and captioned One-to-Many Problem. Panel C shows the same manifold cut by a translucent blue slice, the canonical section. Red Ψ arrows project points onto the slice. Black v_pred and blue u_tgt vectors and the projection ΠH are drawn, with the loss formula in a gray box, captioned One-to-One Problem. The eye goes first to the large captions and the red arrows.
caption: Intuitive overview. (A) We reconstruct 2D or 3D objects by learning the flow from a disordered state to a reconstructed one. (B) Due to global symmetries, many configurations are equivalent, forming redundant “vertical” orbits. Learning on the full space is ambiguous because of unpredictable drift along these orbits. (C) We eliminate this redundancy by fixing a gauge: the mapping Ψ projects configurations onto a unique slice (canonical section) across the orbits, while the operator ΠH projects the gradients (velocities) to remove irrelevant vertical drift. The model thus learns only meaningful “horizontal” motions that change the shape.
abstract: Reassembling $N$ fragments in $n$-dimensional space is a shape reconstruction task that is invariant to global rigid motions. Training directly on $\mathcal{M}=\mathrm{SE}(n)^N$ can be ill-posed: standard losses penalize solutions that differ only by a global transform. Existing methods often address this with ad-hoc anchoring which breaks permutation invariance across fragments and can introduce biases that must be mitigated with extensive and costly data augmentation. We propose a geometric framework that enforces invariance by construction. First, a **Global Gauge Fixing** (GGF) strategy deterministically aligns configurations using an intrinsic generalized-inertia rule. Second, we introduce a **quotient-invariant Flow Matching objective** that operates via orthogonal projection onto the horizontal tangent bundle. This construction factors out global pose at each timestep, enabling the model to learn only shape-changing dynamics on the quotient space $\mathcal{M}/\mathrm{SE}(n)$. Our unified $\mathrm{SE}(n)$-invariant framework admits efficient closed-form 2D/3D instantiations and improves accuracy on polygonal jigsaw puzzles and 3D fracture reassembly benchmarks.
